question: Should OpenClaw standardize a core skill capability manifest now, and if so which guarantees belong in declarative metadata, ClawHub/install consent, and runtime enforcement?
rationale: The proposal creates a user-facing security promise across untrusted third-party skills; code cannot safely choose the permanent permission vocabulary, enforcement semantics, signing model, or compatibility policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Set a staged capability-manifest RFC
options.body: Define a versioned, inspectable manifest and explicit non-enforcement semantics first, then separately land consent and enforcement phases.

options.title: Prioritize runtime enforcement first
options.body: Design generic enforcement hooks and policy decisions before exposing a manifest that users may treat as a guarantee.

options.title: Keep this external for now
options.body: Document current ClawHub scanning and plugin hooks while allowing experimental skill-security tooling to evolve outside core until a stable contract emerges.

recommendation.title: Set a staged capability-manifest RFC
recommendation.body: Define a versioned, inspectable manifest and explicit non-enforcement semantics first, then separately land consent and enforcement phases.

likelyOwner.reason: The recorded maintainer response already frames the remaining choice as product/security follow-up.
